original: The old man and the sea were one.
translated:
El anciano y el mar eran uno.

This translation aims to preserve the poetic, almost mystical tone of the original English text. The phrase "The old man and the sea were one" suggests a deep spiritual connection between the protagonist and the ocean, conveying a sense of unity and oneness. In Spanish, the simple yet powerful phrase "El anciano y el mar eran uno" achieves a similar effect, using the verb "eran" (were) in the past tense to evoke a sense of timeless unity. The translation maintains the concise, lyrical style of the original while adapting it to the natural rhythms and grammar of Spanish.
